review_scope: Independent round-2 Quality Editor approval. The writer's two corrected sentences were re-checked against the live OpenAI and Anthropic pricing pages on 2026-10-20: both now scope the 125x figure to the eight models of the Strategy 9 table ($0.10 to $12.50) and state that the cited pages list higher rates outside that set, naming gpt-6-astra's $20.00/M long-context input against $10.00/M short context. Claude Opus 4.1 at $15.00/M standard short-context input on the same Anthropic page confirms why the previous unscoped superlative was unsupported. Every other price pair, the Strategy 2/4/7 arithmetic, the AWS 86/88/91% result, the LLMLingua 20x figure, the batch 50%/24h terms, the Magnitude paragraph and its internal link, lastmod and the schema dateModified were re-verified as unchanged and supported. No first-party measurement was run and the article promises no reader-facing dataset or script, so public_artifacts is empty.

claims.note: Headline and description keep the inherited 70% figure; the selection forbids changing it and this run measured no savings. It is a planning figure, not a measured result.
Framing paragraph describing the stacking approach; the only numeric content is the list length and the pricing check date, both of which are stated facts.

The 125x figure is scoped to the eight models in the Strategy 9 table ($0.10 for gpt-6-luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 up to $12.50 for gpt-5.6-cyber) and the sentence says so; it is not presented as the extreme across all models on those pages, which list higher and lower tiers. gpt-6-astra's $20.00/M long-context input against $10.00/M short context, and its $50.00/M output rate, are the listed tier values, named as outside the scoped set; the DeepSeek cache-miss and output rates are from the linked DeepSeek page.
Qualitative waste taxonomy. The $0.10-1.00/M range refers to verified cheap-tier input rates from S1 and S2, not to a measured waste share.
Section heading carries an expected planning range for routing, not a measurement from this run.
Blended-cost statement is arithmetic on verified list rates: moving a 60-70% traffic share from $10.00/M input to $0.10-0.30/M input lowers blended input cost by approximately that share.
Heading percentage reflects the largest verified cache-hit discount (5% of input on Sonnet 5.5), stated as an upper bound.
All cache-hit and cache-write rates are quoted from the linked vendor pages read 2026-10-20, including the 125% five-minute write rate and the one-tenth OpenAI cached-input ratio.

10,000 tokens x 1,000 requests = 10M input tokens/day; at Sonnet 5.5 $2.00/M that is $20.00/day, at $0.10/M cache-hit it is $1.00/day, a $19/day or roughly $570/month saving. The 1,024-token automatic threshold is quoted from the OpenAI caching guide.
Table heading states the check date for the rates below.

The 86% cost, 88% latency and 91% accuracy figures are the AWS blog's own measurements at a 0.75 similarity threshold; the 70% hit-rate sentence is arithmetic, not an AWS result.
Operational steps; the only sourced number is the 0.75 threshold at which AWS reports 91% accuracy.
